The clause 'and it took three passes to see that' narrates a completed transition (how the author arrived at the reading) rather than stating a constraint that still binds — the tense test: a reader who never saw the previous passes loses nothing actionable if the clause is cut. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: (c) Bold-label echo: per the maintainer accept-note at line 109, line 59's '**CRAP and complexity metrics.** CRAP pairs a unit's complexity with its test coverage...' defines rather than restates the label — scored PASS on that reading, as directed. Checked the file's other seven bold-labelled subsections independently: six open on a pronoun ('They'/'It') per the rule's stated exemption; '**TDD.**' is acronym expansion (explicitly exempt); '**Architecture Visibility.** Architecture remains human-owned, but it needs instruments' (line 67) restates only the first of the label's two nouns but immediately adds two substantive claims (ownership + need for instruments) rather than merely restating the label — same defining-not-restating logic as the CRAP passage, so it passes on its own merits. (a) Empty negation: line 7 'He is not defending the old world against the new one' and line 99 'The lesson is not "Clean Code was right all along"' both negate a real, plausible prior reading the passage just set up — not empty. (b) Deictic drumroll: line 19 'This is the mercury problem' resolves by immediately naming the concept — exempt per rule's own carve-out. (d) Citation/appendix duplication: the Sources block glosses are below <!-- maintainer -->, out of writing-class scope.
